title: Aspiration Prophylaxis, Perioperative Medication Management, and Cardiac Risk

steps.title: Mendelson Syndrome Criteria
steps.tx: **Mendelson syndrome risk criteria** define chemical pneumonitis resulting from aspiration of acidic gastric contents during induction or emergence. Severe pulmonary tissue destruction occurs when aspirated gastric juice volume exceeds 0.4 milliliters per kilogram (approximately 25 milliliters in adults) with a pH under 2.5, precipitating immediate bronchospasm, alveolar-capillary membrane disruption, hypoxaemia, and non-cardiogenic pulmonary edema.

steps.title: Aspiration Prophylaxis Regimen
steps.tx: **Pharmacological aspiration prophylaxis** targets both gastric juice acidity and residual volume in high-risk patients, including full stomachs, pregnant parturients, severe obesity, and hiatus hernia. Non-particulate sodium citrate (0.3 molar, 30 milliliters orally) rapidly neutralizes preexisting stomach acid within five minutes without causing lung granuloma formation if aspirated, unlike particulate magnesium or aluminum hydroxide antacids.

steps.title: Metoclopramide Actions
steps.tx: **Prokinetic actions of metoclopramide** stem from central and peripheral dopamine D2 receptor antagonism combined with cholinergic activation and 5-HT4 receptor agonism. Metoclopramide enhances lower esophageal sphincter resting tone, coordinates antroduodenal contractions, and accelerates gastric emptying of liquids into the duodenum without stimulating acid secretion, though it is contraindicated in mechanical intestinal obstruction.

steps.title: Managing Renin-Angiotensin Drugs
steps.tx: **Withholding ACE inhibitors and ARBs** on the morning of major surgery prevents severe, refractory vasoplegic hypotension upon induction of general anaesthesia. Blunting angiotensin II vasoconstrictor mechanisms leaves vascular smooth muscle refractory to conventional alpha-adrenergic agonists like ephedrine and phenylephrine, often mandating emergency infusion of intravenous vasopressin or methylene blue to restore systemic vascular resistance.

steps.title: Perioperative Medication Continuation
steps.tx: **Essential chronic drugs to continue** on the morning of surgery include beta-blockers, statins, clonidine, and most neuropsychiatric agents, ingested with a minimal sip of water. Abrupt cessation of chronic beta-blockers triggers dangerous rebound sympathetic tachycardia, hypertension, and myocardial ischemia, whereas stopping clonidine precipitates life-threatening rebound hypertensive crisis from acute uninhibited norepinephrine surges.

steps.title: Perioperative Anticoagulant Timing
steps.tx: **Anticoagulation interruption guidelines** dictate stopping warfarin five days before elective surgery to achieve an international normalized ratio (INR) under 1.5, bridging with therapeutic low molecular weight heparin in high thrombotic risk patients. Direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) like apixaban and rivaroxaban are held for 48 hours (or 72 hours if renal clearance is impaired) prior to high-bleeding-risk procedures or neuraxial block.

steps.title: Revised Cardiac Risk Index
steps.tx: **Revised Cardiac Risk Index criteria** established by Lee identify six independent predictors of major adverse cardiac events in non-cardiac surgery: high-risk surgical procedure (intraperitoneal, intrathoracic, suprainguinal vascular), history of ischemic heart disease, history of congestive heart failure, history of cerebrovascular disease, preoperative insulin therapy for diabetes mellitus, and preoperative serum creatinine exceeding 2.0 milligrams per deciliter.

left.title: RCRI Zero or One Predictor
points: Estimated major cardiac event rate 0.4 to 0.9 percent
Proceed directly with scheduled elective non-cardiac surgery

right.title: RCRI Two or More Predictors
points: Estimated cardiac complication rate exceeds 6.6 to 11 percent
Postoperative troponin surveillance and invasive monitoring

steps.title: Informed Consent Standards
steps.tx: **Essential elements of anaesthesia consent** demand transparent disclosure of common minor risks (postoperative nausea, sore throat, dental trauma, transient shivering) alongside rare catastrophic complications (anaphylaxis, malignant hyperthermia, awareness under anaesthesia, perioperative stroke, and death). The signed consent document confirms voluntary acceptance of the proposed anaesthetic plan and emergency resuscitation contingencies.
